technical_architecture.reason: Peer-reviewed 300 mm manufacturability evidence and an independently corroborated full-stack delivery, but no published two-qubit-gate fidelity on the foundry process and no independent performance measurement yet.

execution.reason: Delivered a contracted national-lab testbed (late vs the March 2025 target) and advanced to QBI Stage B; both are execution facts, neither is a utility-scale result.

market_utility.reason: No independently measured application-level performance exists anywhere in the ledger for this company; utility is the quantity NQCC and DARPA are still evaluating.

value_capture.reason: Value capture depends on competitive position across at least eleven Stage-B architectures and on unresolved supply-chain structure; too few resolved observations to bound it.

evidence_increasing: Peer-reviewed record-low charge noise on a customized 300 mm CMOS line (npj QI 2024)
NQCC testbed delivery corroborated by the evaluator and independent press (Sep 2025)
Advanced to DARPA QBI Stage B (Nov 2025) — deeper government scrutiny accepted, not passed
evidence_decreasing: Testbed delivery ran late against the programme's March 2025 target
Every performance figure in the ledger is self-measured; none is independent of the company
Two-qubit gate fidelity on the foundry process remains unpublished at Genesis close
unresolved: Does the installed NQCC system demonstrate measured qubit performance, and what does NQCC report?
Can exchange-control demonstrations convert to >99% two-qubit gates under foundry tolerances?
Does co-integrated cryo-CMOS control survive hybrid quantum+classical power dissipation?

next_decisive.resolution: Peer-reviewed or independently measured two-qubit gate fidelity on a 300 mm MOS process

next_decisive.milestone: NQCC evaluation report for the installed testbed

falsifiers: Charge noise or variability under foundry rules prevents >99% two-qubit gates at array scale
Cryo-CMOS control power destroys qubit performance before useful channel density
The NQCC evaluation fails to show usable qubit performance on the delivered system

technical_architecture.reason: Peer-reviewed complete manufacturable component set at record fidelities — but every fidelity is conditional on detection, and system-level loss remains the unmeasured multiplier.

execution.reason: Deepest DARPA evaluation stage of any company; real fab partnership; real infrastructure commitments — offset by announced-not-verified QCC construction.

market_utility.reason: No application-level result exists; the utility-scale question is precisely what Stage C is evaluating.

value_capture.reason: Vertically integrated photonics supply chains have no public comparables to bound capture against.

evidence_increasing: Nature paper: complete manufacturable photonic component set at GlobalFoundries (Feb 2025)
QBI Stage C entry after a year-long ~50-expert evaluation (Feb 2025)
$125M expanded DARPA agreement (Jul 2026) — sustained evaluator commitment
evidence_decreasing: All component fidelities are conditioned on photon detection — the loss budget is the unanswered question

unresolved: What is the end-to-end loss budget at system scale, and does it fit inside the fusion-tolerance threshold?
Does Stage C verification produce a constructed system that operates as designed?
Can cryogenic loading of millions of detectors be engineered at datacenter scale?

next_decisive.resolution: Independent confirmation of construction progress at Brisbane or Chicago

falsifiers: Integrated photon loss cannot reach the fusion-tolerance threshold at the required component counts
